summary: Zwolle runs a zoned, tax-based parking system. The Parkeerverordening Zwolle 2026 (adopted by the council on 16 June 2025, in force since 1 January 2026) and the Verordening Parkeerbelastingen Zwolle 2026 (adopted 15 December 2025) set the rules and prices. In the inner city, street parking is paid Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 23:00 (Sundays 13:00 to 17:00) and costs 4.00 euros for the first hour and 8.00 euros per hour after that, while municipal garages in the ring around the centre and near the station charge 1.50 euros per hour (7.50 euros per day) and the Noordereiland garage in the inner city 3.00 euros per hour (15.00 euros per day). Policy rests on the Parkeerstrategie 2040 (council, 18 December 2023) and the Nota parkeren (council, 31 March 2025): residents' permits are capped (80 to 85 percent of the permit-eligible spaces in most zones), garages are meant to be cheaper than streets, and the Nota plans stepwise tariff increases from 2028 and a step-by-step extension of regulated parking over 2026 to 2030. A draft college decision of 16 June 2026 proposes extending regulated parking to further districts at the end of the first quarter of 2027; the final decision was due in the third quarter of 2026 and its status was not checked. The city owns and runs most large garages (Katwolderplein, Diezerpoort, Noordereiland, Lübeckplein, Pas de Deux, Emmawijk), while Q-Park operates Centrum (323 spaces), Maagjesbolwerk (453) and the P+R at Hanzelaan 101 near the station, whose capacity is 207 on Q-Park's page but 132 in the open-data record; Q-Park's 'from 12 euros per day' and 'from 20 euros per day' prices are advertised starting prices, not a verified tariff. The first new centre mobility hub, Weezenlanden-Noord (426 spaces, underground), is expected to open in 2030 according to a November 2025 council proposal that asked for 7.2 million euros of extra credit, with temporary parking arranged elsewhere in the meantime; in 2023 the college proposed 28.5 million euros for the Nieuwe Veemarkt hubs (about 950 places in the plan). The municipal open-data live feeds for the city garages were last updated in June and July 2025, although the Q-Park P+R record was current on 21 October 2026, and no published utilisation statistics were found. The municipal website zwolle.nl was unavailable (HTTP 429) and was not used.

items.text: The Parkeerverordening Zwolle 2026 (adopted by the council on 16 June 2025) has applied since 1 January 2026 and replaces the Parkeerverordening 2016. It is the framework for resident and business permits and garage subscriptions, and defines the inner city as the area bounded by the Stadsgracht, Schuttevaerhaven and Achtergracht.

The council adopted the Parkeerstrategie 2040 on 18 December 2023 and its elaboration, the Nota parkeren, on 31 March 2025. A draft traffic decision of the college dated 16 June 2026 (to be published on 22 June 2026) cites both dates and says that fiscalised parking (paid parking plus permits on the same spaces) is being introduced in the Hanzeland/Spoorzone district.

The Nota parkeren (March 2025) splits Zwolle into six zones with fiscalised parking (paid parking plus permits) as the standard, progressive street tariffs in zones 1-3 (the hourly price doubles after one or two hours), and a rule that parking in a garage or hub should be cheaper than on the street. Regulated parking is to be extended step by step from the centre outwards in 2026-2030, and the blue-zone parking disc in part of Schellerbroek is planned to end in 2026.

The Aanwijzingsbesluit gereguleerd parkeren 2026 (decided 4 November 2025, in force 1 January 2026) sets paid-parking hours: zone I (inner city) Monday-Saturday 09:00-23:00 and Sunday 13:00-17:00; zones II and IV Monday-Saturday 09:00-20:00 and Sunday 13:00-17:00. Disabled-card holders still have to pay in garages and barrier car parks.

The Regeling parkeervergunningen 2026 caps resident and business permits at 80 percent of the permit-eligible spaces in zone I (85 percent in most of zone II and in zone IV), with a waiting list. Zone I allows at most 25 business permits, and a visitor permit covers 120 hours per quarter.

The council adopted the Verordening Parkeerbelastingen Zwolle 2026 on 15 December 2025 (in force from 19 December 2025). Street parking in zone I (inner city) costs 4.00 euros for the first hour and 8.00 euros per hour from the second; zone II (centrumschil) 2.00 euros for the first two hours and 4.00 euros from the third; zone IV (schil) 1.50 euros per hour. The first resident permit costs 225 euros per year in zone I, 70 euros in zone II and 50 euros in zone IV.
items.source_title: Verordening op de heffing en de invordering van parkeerbelastingen 2026 (CVDR751055)

items.text: In the same 2026 tariff table the municipal Noordereiland garage in the inner city costs 3.00 euros per hour and 15.00 euros per day (lost ticket 42.00 euros). The garages Diezerpoort, Emmawijk, Katwolderplein, Lübeckplein and Pas de Deux and several surface car parks cost 1.50 euros per hour and 7.50 euros per day (lost ticket 16.50 euros).
items.source_title: Verordening op de heffing en de invordering van parkeerbelastingen 2026 (CVDR751055)

items.text: A council document of 16 December 2024 for the 2025 tariff table (its publication dates still show placeholders, so the final published ordinance may differ) set 3.30 euros per hour in the inner city, with payment limited to blocks of 60 minutes between 09:00 and 18:00, and an evening rate of 2.20 euros per hour (maximum 4.40) from 20:00 (Thursdays 21:00) to 23:00. For the Noordereiland garage it set a maximum of 16.50 euros for 09:00-20:00 and 20.90 euros per calendar day (to 23:00). The 2026 table has a single street tariff of 4.00 euros for the first hour and 8.00 euros per hour after that until 23:00, and a 15.00 euro Noordereiland day rate.

The Nota parkeren plans stepwise tariff rises from 2028 (its annex 3 lists them; the 2026 and 2028 tables are to become part of the Tarievennota 2026 and 2028): street parking in zone 1 at 4.50 euros for the first hour and 9.00 euros from the second, garage parking in zone 1 at 3.50 euros per hour and 17.50 euros per day, and a first resident permit of 250 euros. From 2026 all parking tariffs are to be adjusted every two years on the basis of consumer price inflation and other circumstances. These 2028 figures are plans, not tariffs in force.
items.source_title: Nota parkeren Zwolle (gemeente Zwolle, March 2025), annex 3

items.text: A college decision note dated 16 June 2026 sets out a draft decision (not yet final) to extend regulated parking, planned for the end of the first quarter of 2027, to Hogenkamp/Indische buurt, Spoorzone/Hanzeland, Schellerbroek, part of Schellerhoek and Wipstrik Zuid. Draft traffic decisions would end the Schellerbroek parking-disc zone and add a parking-disc zone at the Forelkolk shopping-centre car park (about 70 spaces). Twelve residents' meetings drew about 8 percent of the roughly 3,500 households written to. The note says the final decision had to be taken in the third quarter of 2026 for the 2027 start; whether that has happened was not checked.
items.source_title: Beslisnota Ontwerpbesluit uitbreiding gereguleerd parkeren 2027 (college, 16 June 2026)

items.text: The 2026 designation decision names 12 garages and car parks open to subscription holders, each with a cap on subscriptions, for example Diezerpoort 305, Katwolderplein 350, Emmawijk 176, Turfmarkt 177 and Burgemeester Van Roijensingel 184. The privately run Q-Park Centrum is listed with up to 165 subscriptions for residents and businesses, and the Dijkstraat garage with 49 for residents.

Zwolle's open-data records (RDW NPR register, read 21 October 2026) list the municipality as operator of the garages Katwolderplein (700 spaces), Diezerpoort (611), Noordereiland (330 plus 340 on two levels), Lübeckplein (385), Pas de Deux (204) and Burgemeester Van Roijensingel (190). The municipal live feeds show last updates in June-July 2025, so they appear not to be maintained.
items.source_title: RDW NPR open data, Zwolle municipal facility records

items.text: Q-Park lists three facilities in Zwolle: the garage Centrum at Pletterstraat 41 (323 spaces), the garage Maagjesbolwerk at Maagjesbolwerk 54 (453 spaces) and the P+R at Hanzelaan 101 near the station (207 spaces on Q-Park's own page; the open-data live record gives a capacity of 132, and the two were not reconciled). Its Zwolle page, read on 21 October 2026, advertises 'from' prices of 20 euros per day at Maagjesbolwerk and 12 euros per day at the P+R, but the same page also shows a deal from 16.50 euros per day and a page title 'from 18 euros per day', and the facility tariff tables did not load, so these are advertised starting prices rather than a verified tariff. A rail-traveller discount applies to domestic train journeys under conditions on the P+R page, and online reservation is offered.

Q-Park lists 20 electric charge points at Centrum and 26 at Maagjesbolwerk, and the municipal open-data record for Katwolderplein lists 30. The Nota parkeren counted over 1,100 public charge points in Zwolle (about 50 in municipal car parks), plans at least 100 more in existing garages, and says new developments should have working charge points at 20 percent of spaces on completion; the street-charging concession runs to 1 July 2027.
items.source_title: Q-Park Centrum and Maagjesbolwerk pages (read 21 October 2026); Nota parkeren Zwolle (March 2025)

items.text: According to the Nota parkeren, Zwolle had about 2.5 million parking transactions in 2023, 57 percent of street transactions were made by phone app, and 93 percent of permit requests go through the digital counter. Enforcement uses a scan car (over one million scans), and garages with barriers keep cash payment for now while app payment and reservation are to be added.

The first planned centre mobility hub, Weezenlanden-Noord (underground, below the Luttenbergstraat next to the provincial office), has been reduced to 426 spaces and needs an extra 7.2 million euros of credit. The council proposal of 12 November 2025 expects construction to start in mid-2027 and the hub to open in 2030, with charging at only about 2.5 percent of spaces at opening instead of 20 percent because of grid congestion.

A council letter of 6 May 2025 reported that the college had decided in principle to provide temporary parking while the Weezenlanden-Noord hub is built: a site on the Goertjesweg (an existing car park with room for about 80 places, to be rented, with the lease not yet final), resident parking at the Turfmarkt and 20 extra visitor places on the Schuurmanstraat. The study put the need at 400 spaces in and around the district, and part of the provincial car park closes during construction.
items.source_title: Raadsbrief Locatiebesluit Tijdelijke Parkeervoorziening Weezenlanden-Noord (6 May 2025)

items.text: In October 2023 the college asked the council for 28.5 million euros for the Nieuwe Veemarkt (Kamperpoort) mobility hubs: one of about 225 spaces on the city side and one of about 300 along the A28, with about 950 parking places in the plan overall. The proposal also guarantees 100 replacement places for the existing Emmadek.
items.source_title: Beslisnota Mobiliteitshubs Nieuwe Veemarkt en parkeren (3 October 2023)

gaps: www.zwolle.nl (parkeren, parkeertarieven, parkeergarages, P+R, laadpalen pages) returned HTTP 429 with a 'temporarily offline due to a global security vulnerability' message on 21 October 2026; not worked around, so current municipal web pages on tariffs, garage opening hours and permits could not be read.

No published occupancy or utilisation statistics for Zwolle's garages or the P+R were found (only a 2017 council note describing biennial parking-pressure surveys and the 'Memo parkeerbalans Stadshart 2025', an annex of the May 2025 council letter that was not opened).

The Q-Park web pages for Centrum, Maagjesbolwerk and P+R Zwolle could not load their tariff tables ('tariffs could not be loaded'); only the headline 'from' prices on the Zwolle overview page were readable. Q-Park's page lists 207 spaces for P+R Hanzelaan; the open-data live record declares a different capacity, which could not be reconciled.

The municipal open-data live feeds (RDW NPR) for the city garages show last-update timestamps from June-July 2025, so no current availability data was usable; the tariff blocks in the static NPR records are outdated (2013-2018 validity) and were not used.

Not opened: the full Adaptieve Ontwikkelstrategie Mobiliteitshubs (AOS) and the October 2025 council letter on its financial outlook, the Bereikbaarheidsagenda Binnenstad (only the college response of 28 January 2025 was found in search results, not read), the Mobiliteitsvisie 2019, the Nota mobiliteitsnormen, and the council letter 'Stand van zaken implementatie Nota parkeren' (June 2026).

No local press (De Stentor, Zwolle Nieuws, RTV Oost) or NS/ProRail/province material on station and P+R parking was read: the web search budget was used up, so news coverage, any P+R policy and the provincial car park at the Provinciehuis are not covered beyond the council documents.
The 2025 tariff comparison relies on a council document of 16 December 2024 that still contains placeholder dates (xx); the final published 2025 ordinance was not retrieved.
